source_design.section: 6. Decision (3): clearinghouse.entity_alias (D3.1-D3.8 plus its could-not-decide list)
source_design.note: Chris settled decision (3) on 2026-10-25 and said the mechanism was the design session's to produce. Session f84749dc produced it to PRD-ready precision. This PRD TRANSCRIBES that design; it does not re-decide it.

derivations_beyond_the_source_design: Q2a -- an `observation` field ('present' | 'withdrawn'), making the table SEVEN columns and the fill-only key a five-tuple, so retraction works without a mutable column. THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THE PRD GOES BEYOND CHRIS'S SETTLED DESIGN: section 6 specifies six columns and is silent on retraction. The gap was flagged as a Gotcha, routed to session 793ad471 (KBDL obsolete-ID service, which owns the adjacent rail), and its argument adopted: a retracted_at column would require UPDATING a row (append-only forbids it) and would make withdrawal terminal, when NCBI genuinely un-suppresses accessions. The fill-only interaction that argument did not address is resolved here by splitting observe_alias (always appends) from register_aliases (fill-only, always 'present'); without the split, fill-only silently suppresses reinstatement. Reversible in BOTH directions, unusually: null reads naturally as 'present', so adding it later does not strand rows either. Confidence medium.
Q3 -- a dedicated public register_aliases() verb, because register() routes through table_name() which raises ValueError outside ENTITY_TYPES x _KINDS. Forced by existing code; confidence high.

Q4 -- a fourth manifest block kind with a list-shaped [[source.alias]] block, because D3.7 names TOML-driven backfill adapters as writers and the parameter-set precedent rides inside [source.result] at a cardinality aliases do not share. Fourth-kind decision forced; the exact TOML spelling is unvalidated against any real preset; confidence medium.

Q7 -- resolve() RAISES on a one-pair-to-many-hashes collision rather than choosing. Confidence medium; whether many-to-many is normal in other alias vocabularies is genuinely open and was put to the external scan.

judgement_calls.highest_risk: Q2 -- no confidence/asserted_by column. MEDIUM blast radius at LOW confidence, the only such combination in the document, and the entry the source design itself recorded as the one it was least sure of. Cheapest moment to reverse is before any row exists, which is now.
judgement_calls.most_likely_to_be_reversed: Q2a -- the observation field. Not the highest-risk entry, but the only one that goes beyond Chris's settled design, so it is the one he is most likely to strike. Q2a names exactly what to delete if so.

unresolved_external_facts: Whether any kbaseincubator.fitness row already carries an assembly_hash computed under hash rule B (sha256 of canonical FASTA bytes, order-dependent) rather than rule A (sorted-join entity_hash, order-independent). The design session read the COLUMNS, not the VALUES. If even one row is rule B it is a live data problem and not only a documentation gap, and decision (2) -- the genome companion namespace, built on exactly that column -- inherits it. Settled by one COUNT(*) against fitness.genome joined to a known rule-A hash, or more cheaply by whoever wrote those rows saying which function they called. The parallel question for the GAA store is genome-identity-v1's Q12.2 and is open there too.

At what scale a closed ten-value in-code alias_source vocabulary becomes the wrong call. identifiers.org and Bioregistry exist because closed in-code prefix lists did not scale; this PRD does not know the threshold here, and whether a migration path exists that does not rewrite rows was put to the external scan.
live_facts_are_inherited_not_measured: No live lake read was performed by the authoring session. The 19 objects in kbaseincubator.clearinghouse, the two precedent alias schemas (inner_loop.v2_genome_aliases and fitness.gene_alias), ontology_term_content's namespace column, and the 0-row genome tables are all RECORDS from session f84749dc's read-only pod read at 2026-10-25 17:36 CDT and session 590fd2c5's 17:07 CDT probe. They were roughly six hours old at authoring time and are reported as records, not as present-tense measurements.
acceptance_is_an_operator_step: OP-C5, in-pod, AFTER the tasks merge, and NOT a build task: bootstrap() dry run showing action=create for entity_alias only with the sixteen others already present; the real run; an acceptance read of the live COLUMNS and the live PARTITION SPEC (not merely that the table exists -- bootstrap() cannot add a column to an existing table, so a hand-created wrong-shaped table verifies as present); then `kbu clearinghouse health` exiting ZERO with alias_integrity present and orphan_total 0. In-pod credentials live on kbhub, so the route is Albert's and his to state. UNTIL OP-C5 HAS RUN THIS PRD IS `continue`, NOT `finished` -- the live precedent is kbdl-file-load-and-genome-sources-v1, which has every task merged and is still unfinished because its acceptance is an operator load nobody has run.

coordination_hazard: MATERIALISED DURING THIS SESSION, exactly as predicted. Three workstreams read and write KBUtilLib main concurrently. main moved from b63eb6a2 to ed40f288 mid-authoring. Worse, because the authoring worktree held `main` checked out, the ref moved under it and left its INDEX holding the pre-ed40f28 content of nine files -- a STAGED REVERSION of the H1 fix, verified by blob hash (index == b63eb6a2 blob, != ed40f288 blob). A plain `git commit` in that worktree would have committed the reversion and silently undone another session's landed work. It was handled by ABANDONING that worktree and creating a fresh one at ed40f288 rather than by index surgery, so no stale index or working tree was left behind as a landmine. Every task prompt carries the instruction to re-read main in the same minute its branch is cut; this is why.

cross_session_design_input.793ad471 (KBDL obsolete-ID service): Answered the retraction question this PRD routed to it, and the answer is adopted as Q2a. Also corroborated Q7 independently (its supersession resolver refuses a multi-child id for the same reason) and contributed two refinements now in the body: a DISTINCT AliasAmbiguousError type, and the principle that 'unknown' and 'contested' must never collapse into one answer. It is recording in kbdl-obsolete-id-resolution-v1 that EXTERNAL retraction is deliberately out of its scope and lives here, so the seam is closed by decision rather than by both sides assuming. It also supplied the design note that observed_at is the CORRECT clock for upstream-assertion currency even though it is the wrong clock for object currency.
cross_session_design_input.368c658e (genome companion namespace): Measured fitness.gene_alias at ZERO rows, which CORRECTS and weakens a precedent this PRD's first draft leaned on; folded in with attribution. Asked whether its genome_alias should be a projection of entity_alias -- answered in Q1: genericity is firm so a projection is the right end state, but not yet, because the join key is undeclared (Q11.1), there is no retraction guarantee it can rely on, and orphan aliases are legal. Recommendation sent: build separately now, spell the columns identically, converge via a view rather than a rewrite.

h1_resolved_mid_authoring: H1, the KBDL-object-URI spelling, was RESOLVED AND LANDED while this PRD was being written. Chris chose option A on 2026-10-25, answering the envelope this PRD's authoring lineage raised (20261025T224003), and it landed as KBUtilLib main ed40f28 at 22:54 CDT: both backfill presets now emit obj:// forms and koros_arc_store's _OBJ_URI_RE admits an optional non-empty #<fragment>. So blocked continuation 199 is answered -- it was filed by session f84749dc, which has been notified so it can resolve the row. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS PRD: alias_id stays BARE, but now on positive CURIE-versus-URI grounds rather than because H1 was undecided, and the resulting silently-empty-join hazard against genome_content.fasta_reference is new Gotcha 12 plus a documentation obligation in t7.
